passage:
During a power failure, a hospital used backup systems. Some machines continued working, but computers were limited.
Nurses took notes on paper. Doctors used flashlights and battery-powered tools. The hospital had practiced for such situations.
A medical student watching the event was impressed. She had thought modern medicine depended completely on advanced technology.
A senior nurse said, "Technology is important, but basic skills must remain."
The hospital returned to normal after power was restored.
The event showed that progress should not erase older abilities. In emergencies, low-tech methods can keep high-tech systems from failing completely.
